subject: Follow-up: Model shortlist, TPS snapshots and regression playbook
messages:

Subject: Re: Post-demo — follow ups

Thanks for the demo this morning. Quick notes and a few asks from our side so we can decide pilot scope:

- Primary goal: low-latency customer-facing summarization of product tickets (median latency target ~80ms, p99 under 250ms for 512 tokens).
- Throughput: initial pilot ~50 concurrent users peak (target ~120 TPS at burst).
- Data retention & compliance: we need to confirm whether queries or KV cache persist beyond 7 days and what logs Redwood exposes (audit / trace).

Could you share the specific model candidates you think map to our latency/TPS targets, plus the perf snapshots you mentioned in the call (p50/p95/p99 and TPS numbers)? Also please send the prompt set you used for benchmarking so our engineers can sanity-check on our side.

Appreciate it — Dani

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>

Subject: Follow-up: Model shortlist, TPS snapshots and regression playbook

Hi Danielle — thanks again for the time. Short recap plus what we attached for you:

Recap / alignment:
- Pilot scope: 1-week run with production-like traffic (50 concurrent users, peak bursts to 120 TPS), focusing on ticket summarization and short-form prioritization output.
- SLO targets you shared: median ~80ms, p99 < 250ms for 512-token responses.
- Compliance: we’ll confirm the audit log retention options; by default control-plane logs are 30 days, and customer KV/prefix caches are configurable — Aditya included details below.

What we attached / shared in this thread:
- redwood_perf_profiles_v2.pdf — Redwood-verified performance profiles for candidate models (p50/p95/p99 latency, TPS at common batch sizes, cost per 1k tokens)
- orion_prompt_set_v1.jsonl — the prompt set we used to mirror your ticket samples (sanitized)
- bench_snapshot_20280721.csv — raw TPS/latency samples from our sandbox (512-token workload)

Top recommended slate (tradeoffs summarized):
1) rw-compact-7B-8bit — best cost/perf for median latency; expected median ~60ms, p99 ~220ms at 120 TPS with q8 quantization. Good starting point for pilot.
2) rw-instruct-13B-q4f — better generation quality for edge-case summaries; median ~95ms, p99 ~280ms at comparable TPS (may need fallback policy for p99 spikes).
3) rw-llama-2-70b-fp16 — highest quality; requires dedicated capacity for stable p99 (median ~120ms, p99 ~320ms unless pinned to higher tier). Recommended if you prioritize quality over unit cost.

Quality regression guardrails we recommend for the pilot:
- Baseline prompt set + a small holdout (10% of prompts) used as regression checks every deploy.
- Automatic rollback on quality drop >5% (measured by ROUGE / human-derived label set) or latency p99 increase >30% for two consecutive 5-minute windows.
- Token-level cost budget alerts (notify on 25/50/80% of projected consumption).

Next steps / asks:
- Can you confirm sample volume and whether you can provide a 500–1,000-record holdout (sanitized)?
- Please confirm if procurement needs a redline copy of our pilot addendum (Camila can own) — I added procurement contacts above.
- Proposed follow-up: 30m technical deep-dive next Tue to review bench CSV and integration steps.

Link to perf dashboard (view-only): https://redwood.example.com/perf/dashboards/orn-2027-41
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/ORN-2027-41

Thanks — attaching the profiles and prompt pack below.

Best,
Sofia
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Model shortlist, TPS snapshots and regression playbook

Hi Dani — quick technical notes and the bench excerpts you asked for. See inline and attached CSV snapshot.

Quoted from Sofia: "Top recommended slate (tradeoffs summarized):"
> 1) rw-compact-7B-8bit — best cost/perf for median latency; expected median ~60ms, p99 ~220ms at 120 TPS with q8 quantization.

Details / assumptions we used for those numbers:
- Hardware: A100s and condensed nvlinks in our dedicated pool; sandbox numbers mix A10G and A100 (bench_snapshot_20280721.csv shows per-host lines).
- Sequence length: 512 tokens end-to-end (prompt + completion) — our CSV has a seq_len column.
- Continuous batching: we measured steady-state TPS with batching window tuned to 3–6ms for low-latency workloads.

Key excerpts from bench_snapshot_20280721.csv (summary):
- rw-compact-7B-8bit (q8): median latency 58ms, p95 165ms, p99 218ms at 120 concurrent TPS (batch sizes 1–8 hybrid). TPS stable at 120 for 10 min window.
- rw-instruct-13B-q4f: median 92ms, p95 210ms, p99 278ms at 90–110 TPS (higher variance at sustained 120 TPS).
- rw-llama-2-70b-fp16: median 118ms, p95 260ms, p99 320ms — needs dedicated reserved capacity to avoid p99 spikes.

Notes on caching & retention:
- By default the KV cache is ephemeral per-request and lives only for the model instance lifecycle. We can enable short-lived prefix caching (configurable 24h/7days) — that will reduce end-to-end cost for repeated queries but is optional for pilot.
- Control-plane audit logs: 30 days by default (exportable). We offer a SOC2-ready evidence pack to share with procurement; Camila / procurement can request specific retention SLAs.

Regression monitoring suggestions (practical):
- Run daily mini-regressions (100 holdout prompts) using ROUGE-L and a small human spot-check for hallucination rate.
- Add a latency sentinel that triggers at p99 > 275ms (for the compact model) to flip traffic to a fallback model (rw-instruct-13B-q4f) while we investigate.

Attachments: bench_snapshot_20280721.csv (CSV — per-host latency/TPS samples)

If helpful I can join the deep-dive to walk through the CSV and config toggles (autoscaling, batch windows, fallback routing).

Cheers,
Aditya
Senior ML Engineer — Redwood Inference
